headline: Boston College Ground Game Overwhelms Miami's Struggling Offense
body: Boston College's balanced attack proved too much for Miami's defense to handle Saturday, as the Eagles rolled to a 29-15 victory behind a dominant rushing performance. Sam Leavitt orchestrated the win with surgical precision, completing 22 of 29 passes for 218 yards and two touchdowns, but it was the ground game that set the tone early and never relinquished control. Boston College totaled 155 rushing yards on the day, a stark contrast to Miami's anemic 55 yards on the ground, establishing a physical advantage that persisted throughout the contest.

Miami's offense sputtered despite clean execution in the turnover department. Quarterback Mertz managed 225 passing yards and a touchdown on 23 completions, but the Hurricanes' inability to establish any semblance of rushing attack forced them into obvious passing situations that Boston College's defense could predict and contain. Wide receiver Dike's five receptions for 48 yards represented Miami's most reliable target, yet the offense lacked the explosive plays needed to sustain drives. The Eagles controlled the line of scrimmage on both sides, limiting Miami to 280 total yards while generating 357 of their own.

Boston College's approach was methodical and relentless. Running back Clark churned out 80 yards on 10 carries, setting up manageable third-down situations that Leavitt converted with his two touchdown passes. Wide receiver Flemming was the most dynamic playmaker on the field with six catches for 76 yards and two scores, providing the vertical threat that kept Miami's secondary honest. The Eagles' balanced attack prevented any single defensive scheme from taking hold, and Miami simply never found an answer to the Eagles' rhythm.
turningPoint: Boston College's second-quarter touchdown drive, featuring three consecutive running plays that moved the chains and culminated in a Leavitt touchdown pass to Flemming, shifted momentum decisively in the Eagles' favor and exposed Miami's inability to adjust to ground-heavy offensive schemes.

unsungHero.name: Flemming
unsungHero.why: While Leavitt earned Player of the Game honors for his decision-making and efficiency, Flemming's dual-threat capacity—both as a receiver and red-zone target—was arguably more disruptive to Miami's defensive gameplan and directly responsible for two of Boston College's three passing touchdowns.
